subject: health
topic: Your 'Safe' drinking water may contain endocrine disrupting chemicals
angle: While PFAS are linked to endocrine disruption and are found in drinking water for millions of people, pharmaceutical residues are only detected in drinking water in a few cases.
title: The Chemicals in Your Water

hooks.text: Is your tap water affecting your hormones?
You assume your water is pure. The data shows otherwise.
You are drinking chemicals that disrupt your reproductive health.
A clear glass of water on a kitchen counter.
6 million residents exceed health limits for pfos and pfoa.

reveal.headline: Millions of people drink water containing endocrine disruptors.
reveal.body: Drinking water for 6 million u.s. residents exceeds health advisories for pfos and pfoa. These substances are linked to endocrine and reproductive health risks.

explain.headline: The chemicals are widespread.
explain.body: Per- and poly-fluoroalkyl substances are found in water supplies worldwide. They interfere with normal reproductive function and hormonal signaling. However, pharmaceutical residues are only detected in a few cases.

matters.headline: The unseen influence on your body.
matters.body: These chemicals are part of your daily environment. That may be why your internal hormonal signaling is affected by sources you cannot see or taste.

example.headline: A glass of water.
example.body: You pour a glass of water from the tap in your kitchen. It looks clear. It tastes neutral. It is part of your daily routine.

verdict: The evidence confirms that PFAS are widespread in drinking water and linked to endocrine and reproductive issues, but the presence of pharmaceuticals in drinking water is much less common.
caveat: The research notes that the specific mechanisms of action for PFAS in the female reproductive and endocrine systems are not yet evident.
caption:
Your drinking water may contain hidden chemicals. 

Research shows that PFAS are widespread in water supplies and linked to endocrine and reproductive issues. However, the specific mechanisms of action for these chemicals in the female reproductive system are not yet evident. 

Does your water supply have these contaminants?
